allowed_losses.AEGS_Tiburon: EXPECTED, declared by C1 on 2026-08-29 for the rebuild that caused it. The scale rule matches CIG's Length to the model's Z extent, and on 19 of 258 models Z is not the long axis - the Mantis measures 1680 x 2965 x 630, which is not the shape of a ship. Ten hulls were drawing every dot in a heap the size of a cockpit while the page labelled them 'cig'; the Tiburon put all 17 in one clump, measured by photographing all 295 ships. Placement now REFUSES a model whose orientation it cannot establish rather than guessing which axis is the length. Hulls that had ONLY CIG dots lose them entirely; the rest fall back to name-derived estimates, which the page labels honestly. Four (Pitbull, Railen, San'tok.yai, Reliant) looked plausible and are refused anyway - same wrong axis, and looking right is not proof. docs/FINDING_the-dots-were-in-a-heap-2026-08-28.md + checks/_verify_marker_spread.py. REMOVE THIS when the models are re-exported in a known orientation - a declaration that outlives its reason is how a real loss gets waved through.

how_to_declare_a_loss: put the class in allowed_losses with a sentence saying WHY it is expected. It is printed on every run afterwards, so a declared loss stays visible instead of becoming invisible.
what: markers per hull in testing/_deploy/loadout_marker.gen.js, recorded so a later build cannot lose a hull quietly
